newsitem.title: MALAYSIA: Malaysian firms to jointly build high-tech city.
newsitem.headline: Malaysian firms to jointly build high-tech city.

text.p: Three Malaysian companies said on Wednesday that they and a businessman will form a joint venture firm to develop a high-technology township with gross development value of 23.8 billion ringgit.

Conglomerate Renong Bhd, property firm Country Heights Holdings Bhd and hotel developer Landmarks Bhd said in separate statements they and Mustapha Kamal Abu Bakar will be involved in developing Cyberjaya.
The four is forming joint venture firm Setia Haruman Sdn Bhd on an equal 25 percent equity basis.
Separately, Setia has entered into a joint venture agreement with four other firms and the Selangor state government to form the Cyberview Sdn Bhd consortium to build the 2,800 hectare city.
Cyberview was appointed by the Malaysian government to develop Cyberjaya, located within Malaysia's planned information technology zone, the Multimedia Super Corridor (MSC).
The MSC, which hopes to attract global leading edge multimedia firms, is an investment zone located in central Selangor state.
The four firms are government-owned Multimedia Development Corp Sdn Bhd, Golden Hope Plantations Bhd, Nippon Telegraph and Telephone Corp and state fund Permodalan Nasional Bhd.
